title: Which button? World trust vs the red/blue dilemma
subtitle: Country-level trust, altruism and population, with per-country model outputs
description:
Country-level generalized trust, an assumed altruism constant, and 2022 population for 23 surveyed countries plus a rest-of-world bucket — together with the per-country outputs of the population-scale model those inputs feed, for Tim Urban's red/blue button dilemma ([the tweet](https://x.com/waitbutwhy/status/2047710215265730755)). The model itself and the full write-up are in the companion notebook [Which button?](https://www.kaggle.com/code/axelst/which-button); this page documents the data.

# Files

## countries.csv — model inputs

24 rows: 23 surveyed countries plus `Rest of world`, a ~2.7B-person bucket for nations without an individual trust measurement.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| `code` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; empty for the rest-of-world bucket |
| `iso2` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, lowercase |
| `name` | display name |
| `trust` | share answering "most people can be trusted" (0–1), World Values Survey Wave 7 Q57; Denmark from the European Values Study 2017 |
| `altruism` | assumed altruism weight (0–1); the global dictator-game mean 0.28 on every row |
| `population` | 2022 population, UN World Population Prospects, rounded to the nearest 100k |

## results.csv — model outputs

One row per `countries.csv` entry, computed at the baseline parameters (altruism 0.28, Beta concentration 7, lambda 1, no misclick).

| column | description |
|---|---|
| `blue_fraction` | probability an agent of this country presses blue; equals its death rate while blue loses globally |
| `deaths_per_100k` | `blue_fraction` × 100,000 |
| `deaths_in_global_game` | deaths realized in the single global game |
| `local_win` | whether blue reaches 50% inside this country alone |
| `critical_altruism_self_save` | mean altruism at which this country's blue share crosses 50%; empty where unreachable even at altruism 1.0 |

## world_summary.csv — the aggregate

A single row: the four model parameters, total population, global blue fraction, whether blue wins, world death rate, absolute world deaths, China's share of the toll, the trust a uniform world would need to survive, and the global mean altruism that would flip the world to blue-wins (empty = unreachable).

## sensitivity.csv — parameter sweeps

World outcome under one-at-a-time sweeps. `parameter` is one of `china_trust`, `altruism`, `lambda`, `concentration`, `trust_delta`; `value` is the swept setting; the remaining columns give the resulting world death rate, global blue fraction, and blue-wins flag.

## countries.json

The original input file; its `_meta` block documents every source and caveat verbatim.

# Provenance

- **Trust** — [World Values Survey Wave 7 (2017–2022)](https://www.worldvaluessurvey.org/WVSDocumentationWV7.jsp), Q57, share answering "most people can be trusted", rounded to the nearest percent. Denmark is not in Wave 7; its figure comes from the [European Values Study 2017](https://europeanvaluesstudy.eu/methodology-data-documentation/survey-2017/full-release-evs2017/), merged into the same series.
- **Altruism** — [Engel 2011](https://homepage.coll.mpg.de/pdf_dat/2010_07online.pdf), meta-analysis of dictator games (129 papers, 41,433 observations), global mean transfer ~28%.
- **Population** — [UN World Population Prospects 2022](https://population.un.org/wpp/).

# Limitations

- WVS percentages move 1–3 points between releases as the dataset is curated; values here are approximate.
- China's 64% is unusually high relative to comparable countries and is contested in the literature; it may reflect in-group framing of "most people" rather than generalized trust. Any population-weighted aggregate leans heavily on it.
- `altruism` is a single global constant, not a per-country measurement, and dictator-game giving is a money-sharing proxy, not a willingness-to-die measure.
- The rest-of-world trust (0.18) is a rough average of available regional data; treat it as a lower bound.

Generated by [github.com/4esv/red-blue-buttons](https://github.com/4esv/red-blue-buttons) (`python -m scripts.export_kaggle`).
